summary: This section explains what happens to the property, debts, contracts, and legal cases of an inter-state co-operative society when it transforms into a Producer Company. On the date of transformation, all assets, liabilities, and ongoing legal matters automatically transfer to the new company. Essentially, the Producer Company steps directly into the shoes of the old co-operative society.
points: All movable and immovable properties of the co-operative society vest in the Producer Company on the transformation date.
All rights, debts, liabilities, obligations, and contracts of the old society are transferred to and become those of the Producer Company.
Any money due to the old society is treated as money due to the Producer Company.
The Producer Company takes over the management of any organization previously managed by the old society, and continues any financial, managerial, or technical assistance as needed.
The capital of the former co-operative society becomes part of the capital of the Producer Company.
Any pending lawsuits or legal proceedings involving the old society do not stop and may be continued by or against the Producer Company.
example: Meera Textiles Co-operative Society decided to transform into a Producer Company named Meera Textiles Producer Limited. On the exact date of transformation, all the factory buildings, machinery, and bank balances belonging to the old society automatically became the property of Meera Textiles Producer Limited. Furthermore, a pending court case filed by a supplier against the old co-operative society did not end or get cancelled. Instead, the supplier and Meera Textiles Producer Limited continued the legal proceeding in the exact same manner as before the transformation.

terms.meaning: Giving legal ownership of property or rights to someone.
The process of changing from an inter-state co-operative society into a Producer Company.
To become void or come to an end, specifically referring to a legal lawsuit.

watch: People often think that transforming into a new company cancels old debts or stops ongoing lawsuits, but this law ensures they simply transfer to the new entity.
